reponse:
**What broke:** On Thursday Nov 12, customer dashboards showed stale data from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC (3h40) [1]. Release ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB [1]. With the 512 Mi memory limit, the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped. The change went to all pods at once [1].

Nobody was alerted to the lag. The first signal was a Sentry out-of-memory alert at 09:14 [1]. The team rolled back to v2.13.3 at 10:05, and the lag fully drained at 12:27 [1].

**Data loss:** No. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late [1]. Lior's reconciliation on Nov 13 found that event counts per workspace match the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [5]. All workspaces had delayed dashboards, and 4 customers contacted support [1].

**What we're changing:**
- ingest#419 is merged. It reverts the default to 1 MB. It also adds a memory guard, so the batcher refuses a batch larger than 25% of the container memory limit [9][1]. The bulk import path keeps 10 MB through explicit config [9].
- KES-431: page the on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes. Owner Noa, due Nov 20 [1][6].
- KES-432: ingest config changes go to a canary pool first. Owner Daniel, due Nov 27 [1].
- KES-433: raise the worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes. Owner Lior, due Nov 27 [1].

Orbitly has asked for a service credit for this incident. Sam is checking the terms with finance [3].
